speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for bringing your husband in. To begin, can you describe the specific behaviors you've observed that seem bizarre or agitated? Have there been any recent changes in his sleep, appetite, or substance use?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the delusions of persecution and control are quite specific. Did he experience any auditory or visual hallucinations, and has he had any history of similar episodes or family history of psychiatric disorders? REQUEST TEST: Basic Metabolic Panel, CBC, Thyroid Function Tests, Urine Drug Screen.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Basic Metabolic Panel: Sodium 138 mmol/L, Potassium 4.2 mmol/L, Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, Glucose 95 mg/dL; CBC: WBC 7,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 230,000 /μL; Thyroid Function Tests: NORMAL READINGS; Urine Drug Screen: Alcohol Negative, Amphetamines Negative, Cannabinoids Negative, Cocaine Negative, Opiates Negative.

speaker: Patient
text: creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your urgency. Given the fixed delusions of conspiracy and control, the decline in functioning, and the onset within 6 months, the clinical picture strongly points toward a primary psychotic disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia.
